record.title: Angular progress and normalized energy proportionality
record.one_line_meaning: Angular progress and normalized energy proportionality
formal_core: **Hadi:** We wrote the wave system once in zero-frame Gam and Tick units and once in our local Gam and Tick units. I think we left out something important: angular velocity.
**Assistant:** The missing quantity is not merely another column in the unit table. It can connect wavelength, period, frequency, energy, and phase advance through one common angular ledger.
**Hadi:** Let me define what I mean.
The zero-frame electromagnetic wave whose wavelength is one Gam and whose period is one Tick completes one full circle of angular progress during that wave.
If another wave has twice the wavelength, its angular velocity is one half of the first wave.
During one zero-frame Tick, it completes only one half of a circle.
If the wavelength is 360 times larger, its angular velocity is $1/360$ of the zero-frame reference wave. During one zero-frame Tick, it advances by only $1/360$ of a complete circle.
**Assistant:** This defines angular progress relative to the fundamental reference Tick.

Let the zero-frame reference wave satisfy $$\lambda_0=1\,\mathrm{Gam}_0,
\qquad
T_0=1\,\mathrm{Tick}_0.$$
For a wave with $$\lambda=n\,\mathrm{Gam}_0,$$ the propagation condition gives $$T=n\,\mathrm{Tick}_0.$$
Thus the wave does not lose its complete $2\pi$ phase cycle over its own full period. Rather, it completes only $1/n$ of that cycle during one fundamental reference Tick.
